question: What is the primary purpose of monitoring injection safety devices in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To calculate monthly staff salaries for the pharmacy department
options.B: To prevent infection transmission and occupational injuries
options.C: To determine the total electricity consumption of the clinic
options.D: To evaluate the culinary hygiene of the hospital cafeteria

explanation: Routine surveillance of injection devices ensures safe administration practices, directly minimizing the risk of bloodborne pathogen spread and needlestick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why is monthly monitoring particularly crucial in resource-constrained healthcare environments?

options.A: It guarantees that patients never experience pain during injections
options.B: It prevents supply chain gaps and the use of substandard materials
options.C: It automatically generates international funding for the facility
options.D: It replaces the need for any clinical supervision or training

explanation: Regular checks help catch missing supplies, expired stock, or broken safety equipment before they compromise patient and staff safety. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h1)

question: What metric is typically evaluated by comparing safety boxes used to total injection devices expended?
explanation: Tracking the ratio of safety boxes to syringes ensures that all generated sharps waste is safely contained and accounted for. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h2)

question: How do inventory metrics on the monitoring form assist facility managers?

options.A: By scheduling annual leave for the administrative staff
options.B: By determining the architectural layout of the new ward
options.C: By dictating the exact clinical diagnosis for every admitted patient
options.D: By identifying consumption trends to prevent stockouts of safety devices

explanation: Reviewing opening and closing balances highlights usage rates, enabling accurate forecasting and timely reordering of essential medical supplies. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h2)

question: Where are explanations for stock discrepancies or supply chain bottlenecks typically recorded on the monitoring form?

options.C: In the dedicated remarks section at the bottom
options.D: On the front cover of the patient's medical folder

explanation: The remarks section provides qualitative context for numerical discrepancies or unusual supply chain events during the reporting period. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h3)

question: What information belongs in the header section of the monitoring form?

options.A: Laboratory reference ranges for routine blood investigations
options.B: Detailed clinical histories of patients who received injections
options.C: Facility metadata such as ward name, reporting month, and officer name
options.D: Financial statements and operational budgets of the hospital

explanation: Headers identify the origin and timeframe of the data, ensuring accountability and proper filing of the document. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h3)

question: What is the defining characteristic of an Auto-Disable (AD) syringe?

options.A: It features a detachable needle that can be replaced mid-procedure
options.B: It can be sterilized in an autoclave multiple times without damage
options.C: It locks or breaks automatically after a single injection to prevent reuse
options.D: It changes color when exposed to direct sunlight for over an hour

explanation: AD syringes incorporate a built-in mechanism that renders them permanently inoperable immediately after the plunger is fully depressed. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h4)

question: A nurse is auditing disposal containers on the ward. Which container is appropriate for collecting used syringes and needles?

options.B: A cardboard box used for drug packaging
options.C: An open plastic basin on the treatment trolley

explanation: Sharps must be discarded directly into rigid, puncture-resistant containers specifically manufactured to prevent accidental needle punctures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h4)

question: When should the physical inventory count of injection devices be conducted for the monthly report?

options.A: At the beginning of the calendar year
options.B: On the last working day of the month
options.C: Whenever a new batch of drugs arrives

explanation: Physical verification must occur at the close of the reporting period to ensure the recorded numbers reflect actual inventory on hand. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h5)

question: What is the correct mathematical relationship for inventory reconciliation on the monitoring form?

options.A: Opening Balance plus Receipts minus Consumption equals Closing Balance
options.B: Consumption plus Closing Balance minus Receipts equals Opening Balance
options.C: Opening Balance plus Consumption minus Receipts equals Closing Balance
options.D: Closing Balance plus Receipts minus Opening Balance equals Consumption

explanation: Inventory tracking relies on starting stock, adding new receipts, subtracting what was used, to arrive at the final physical count. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h5)

question: What common error frequently undermines the accuracy of injection safety data reports?

options.A: Using black ink instead of blue ink on the paper form
options.B: Writing the name of the facility in capital letters
options.C: Laminating the completed report before submission
options.D: Transposing digits and failing to record damaged stock

explanation: Simple clerical mistakes like number transpositions or ignoring broken items distort true consumption and inventory data. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h6)

question: What action should a supervisor take when recorded injection consumption vastly exceeds patient attendance numbers?

options.A: Discard the monitoring form and invent new estimated numbers
options.B: Ignore the difference since the supplies are already spent
options.C: Trigger an internal audit to investigate potential discrepancies
options.D: Punish the junior staff without reviewing the register

explanation: Unexplained gaps between patient volume and device use warrant structured investigation to identify waste, loss, or recording errors. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h6)

question: To whom is the completed injection safety monitoring form typically submitted first in a Primary Health Care facility?

options.A: The West African College of Nursing
options.B: The Local Government Area Immunization or Disease Control Officer
options.C: The Federal Minister of Health in Abuja
options.D: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency

explanation: Primary health facilities route their decentralized reports through designated LGA health officers for collation and higher-level review. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h7)

question: Why is strict adherence to monthly submission deadlines essential for supply chain management?

options.A: It prevents patients from visiting the clinic on weekends
options.B: It satisfies legal requirements for annual tax documentation
options.C: It allows logisticians to aggregate data and prevent regional stockouts
options.D: It ensures that hospital security personnel receive their bonuses

explanation: Timely reports enable central authorities to monitor consumption patterns and deploy resupply shipments before facilities run out of stock. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h7)
